title: Gedung Kesenian Jakarta
excerpt: A new visual identity for Gedung Kesenian Jakarta — drawing from the theatre's ornamental colonial architecture to craft a mark that holds across business cards, event tickets, and printed stationery.
overview: Gedung Kesenian Jakarta is one of Indonesia's oldest surviving acoustic theatres — built in 1821 under the Dutch East Indies colonial administration, it has hosted everything from Javanese wayang to contemporary dance and international opera. The brief was an academic identity redesign: modernise the institution's visual language without erasing two centuries of cultural gravity.
challenge: The existing mark sat in an uncomfortable middle — neither contemporary nor genuinely historical. The new system had to work across intimate print touchpoints (tickets, stationery, business cards) and formal public-facing applications, all while drawing honestly from the building's Dutch colonial ornamental ironwork rather than generic 'heritage' signals.
process: Research into the theatre's 1821 founding and its role across three centuries of Jakarta's cultural life
Mark development derived from the building's ornamental ironwork — a woven interlacing motif resolved into a repeating monogram
Palette drawn from the interior: warm ivory, oxidised gold, deep charcoal
Application testing across business cards, event tickets, and printed stationery
outcome: A full identity system anchored by a monogram that doubles as a surface pattern. The mark reads cleanly as a standalone lockup on business card fronts and expands into a textile-like grid on collateral reverses — the same geometry earning its keep at both scales.
reflection: Working without a client brief forced a different discipline: self-imposed constraints instead of stakeholder approvals. The decision to derive the surface pattern directly from the monogram — rather than designing them as separate elements — was the most consequential call and the one that took longest to resolve.

title: The Dharmawangsa Square
excerpt: Brand identity for The Dharmawangsa Square — a lifestyle mall in Kebayoran Baru whose mark draws from the Mahabharata, referencing Yudhisthira's trident and the bond of the five Pandavas.
overview: The Dharmawangsa Square is a lifestyle retail destination in Kebayoran Baru, South Jakarta. The rebranding commission came from a repositioning ambition — moving the property from standard Jakarta mall to curated destination. The name itself carries literary weight: Dharmawangsa, the righteous king of the Mahabharata.
challenge: Translating a Sanskrit epic into a retail identity without producing pastiche. The mark had to carry cultural literacy — immediately readable to those who know the Mahabharata, simply elegant to those who don't — and hold at every scale, from embroidered uniform badges to carved glass entrance panels two metres tall.
process: Brand audit of the existing identity and competitive landscape within the South Jakarta lifestyle segment
Iconographic research into the Mahabharata — Yudhisthira's spear and the five Pandava brothers as the structural motif
Mark construction: crown-spear form in a stylised ornamental lockup, stress-tested at embroidery scale and at carved-installation scale
Wayfinding system developed with the motif carried through directional plates, entrance panels, and internal signage poles
outcome: A complete brand system deployed across exterior signage, interior wayfinding, staff uniforms, and carved frosted-glass entrance installations. The navy and gold palette reads as quiet authority — deliberately distinct from the louder retail identity conventions of the category.
reflection: The wayfinding brief surfaced the sharpest constraint: the same mark that reads cleanly at business-card scale had to survive being carved into a two-metre glass panel. That forced more geometry and less ornament than the initial concept directions allowed.
